data.title: Results: Bilibili Inc. Exceeded Expectations And The Consensus Has Updated Its Estimates
data.description:
Investors in Bilibili Inc. (NASDAQ:BILI) had a good week, as its shares rose 7.8% to close at US$11.43 following the release of its third-quarter results. Bilibili reported CN¥8.3b in revenue, roughly in line with analyst forecasts, although statutory earnings per share (EPS) of CN¥1.14 beat expectations, being 7.6% higher than what the analysts expected. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. We thought readers would find it interesting to see the analysts latest (statutory) post-earnings forecasts for next year.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

After the latest results, the 32 analysts covering Bilibili are now predicting revenues of CN¥35.6b in 2027. If met, this would reflect a solid 11% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to shoot up 36% to CN¥5.23. In the lead-up to this report, the analysts had been modelling revenues of CN¥36.1b and earnings per share (EPS) of CN¥5.50 in 2027. The analysts seem to have become a little more negative on the business after the latest results, given the small dip in their earnings per share numbers for next year.

See our latest analysis for Bilibili

The average price target fell 18% to US$20.30, with reduced earnings forecasts clearly tied to a lower valuation estimate. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. The most optimistic Bilibili analyst has a price target of US$35.97 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at US$11.40. Even so, with a relatively close grouping of estimates, it looks like the analysts are quite confident in their valuations, suggesting Bilibili is an easy business to forecast or the the analysts are all using similar assumptions.

One way to get more context on these forecasts is to look at how they compare to both past performance, and how other companies in the same industry are performing. It's pretty clear that there is an expectation that Bilibili's revenue growth will slow down substantially, with revenues to the end of 2027 expected to display 8.8% growth on an annualised basis. This is compared to a historical growth rate of 11% over the past five years. By way of comparison, the other companies in this industry with analyst coverage are forecast to grow their revenue at 18% per year. So it's pretty clear that, while revenue growth is expected to slow down, the wider industry is also expected to grow faster than Bilibili.

The Bottom Line

The biggest concern is that the analysts reduced their earnings per share estimates, suggesting business headwinds could lay ahead for Bilibili. On the plus side, there were no major changes to revenue estimates; although forecasts imply they will perform worse than the wider industry. The consensus price target fell measurably, with the analysts seemingly not reassured by the latest results, leading to a lower estimate of Bilibili's future valuation.

With that said, the long-term trajectory of the company's earnings is a lot more important than next year. At Simply Wall St, we have a full range of analyst estimates for Bilibili going out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here..

You can also see our analysis of Bilibili's Board and CEO remuneration and experience, and whether company insiders have been buying stock.

data.title: 3 ETFs For Owning Moderna After Its Melanoma Trial Whipsaw
data.description:
You can own Moderna directly and carry the company’s full ride in your account, or you can hold it through a fund that owns many businesses at once. Simply Wall St flags recent heavy insider selling and a very jumpy share price over the last three months. An exchange traded fund that includes Moderna spreads how much those swings affect your portfolio, and also spreads out any gains from the stock.

Moderna just saw its shares spike after positive test results for a melanoma vaccine used with a cancer drug, followed by a pullback as investors weighed future costs and questions on how broadly the treatment might work. That kind of mixed but important news is why some investors look at iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB), VanEck Biotech ETF (BBH), or iShares Genomics Immunology and Healthcare ETF (IDNA) as ways to own Moderna inside a wider mix of healthcare stocks.

Rather choose individual stocks than a fund? Explore 37 high quality undervalued stocks.

iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB)

Gilead Sciences and Amgen anchor the top of IBB, alongside other biotechnology stocks such as Vertex Pharmaceuticals. You get most of your exposure in this ETF to biotechnology at 88.2% of the portfolio, with extra coverage in life sciences tools and services and a smaller slice in pharmaceuticals. Within that mix, Moderna is a meaningful position. It ranks fifth in the fund at 5.67% of assets, so roughly US$57 of every US$1,000 in IBB tracks Moderna rather than the wider biotech group.

Simply Wall St highlights significant insider selling at Moderna over the past three months, which can worry some investors when they own the single stock. IBB cannot blunt that specific concern, since Gilead Sciences, Amgen and many other holdings operate in the same broad sector and face their own management decisions. What you do gain with IBB is exposure to hundreds of biotechnology and related healthcare businesses instead of tying everything to Moderna alone.

Not every stock inside IBB is priced the same way. Find out how many of IBB's holdings look undervalued.

VanEck Biotech ETF (BBH)

BBH gives Moderna a real slice of your biotech allocation at 7% of the portfolio, so US$70 of every US$1,000 tracks the stock. The rest of the ETF looks a lot like IBB, with heavy exposure to biotechnology alongside life sciences tools and services. Amgen is much larger here at 16.8%, and Gilead Sciences also has a double digit weight, so your money leans toward a tight group of big biotech stocks rather than a very broad spread.

Moderna has had a volatile share price over the past three months compared to the US market, and BBH only partly softens that because over 80% of assets sit in the same biotechnology industry and can move together. This means the fund spreads your risk across several large drug developers but leaves the sector’s ups and downs largely intact.

Uncover whether BBH has kept pace with the market over the past week, year and five years

iShares Genomics Immunology and Healthcare ETF (IDNA)

IDNA tilts heavily toward biotechnology at 68.3% of assets, with another 27.2% in pharmaceuticals and a smaller slice in life sciences tools and services. Moderna sits right at the top of that mix, with about US$140 of every US$1,000 in the fund tied to the stock, so it is a real part of what you would own. The balance comes from other healthcare specialists such as Genmab and Twist Bioscience, which pull more of your money into different approaches to genomics and immunology than Moderna alone.

One question with Moderna is how reliably its products can support the business over time. IDNA spreads that risk across companies whose revenue leans on other treatment areas and markets, which can help if Moderna hits a rough patch. A large chunk of the ETF still depends on a narrow group of high science healthcare stocks, so you are ultimately counting on that whole corner of the market to keep delivering.

Ten companies make up 51.6% of IDNA. Find out which ones, and how much each carries.

Choosing how much Moderna you really want

The choice across IBB, BBH and IDNA comes down to how tightly you want to link your money to Moderna after that headline grabbing melanoma trial jump and pullback. IDNA is the most concentrated on the stock, with about US$140 of every US$1,000 going into Moderna, and the highest fee at roughly US$47 a year on a US$10,000 holding. BBH lands in the middle. You pay about US$35 a year in fees and get around US$70 in Moderna for every US$1,000, inside a 27 stock biotech heavy fund.

IBB spreads your risk widest, with 248 holdings and roughly US$57 of every US$1,000 tied to Moderna, although the fund still leans on biotech and related healthcare businesses. That breadth can matter if Moderna’s share price swings sharply again, given Simply Wall St flags recent volatility against the US market. Your decision is simple. If you want the strongest focus on Moderna you look closer to IDNA. If you prefer more companies around it for the same dollar, IBB sits at the other end, with BBH as a concentrated middle ground.

With 16.8% of BBH riding on Amgen, its next few years matter as much as the fund's. See the earnings forecasts for Amgen.

data.title: Here's Why We're Wary Of Buying Deswell Industries' (NASDAQ:DSWL) For Its Upcoming Dividend
data.description:
Some investors rely on dividends for growing their wealth, and if you're one of those dividend sleuths, you might be intrigued to know that Deswell Industries, Inc. (NASDAQ:DSWL) is about to go ex-dividend in just 4 days. The ex-dividend date occurs one day before the record date, which is the day on which shareholders need to be on the company's books in order to receive a dividend. The ex-dividend date is of consequence because whenever a stock is bought or sold, the trade takes at least one business day to settle. Meaning, you will need to purchase Deswell Industries' shares before the 2nd of December to receive the dividend, which will be paid on the 23rd of December.

The company's next dividend payment will be US$0.10 per share. Last year, in total, the company distributed US$0.20 to shareholders. Last year's total dividend payments show that Deswell Industries has a trailing yield of 6.6% on the current share price of US$3.03. Dividends are a major contributor to investment returns for long term holders, but only if the dividend continues to be paid. So we need to investigate whether Deswell Industries can afford its dividend, and if the dividend could grow.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Dividends are typically paid from company earnings. If a company pays more in dividends than it earned in profit, then the dividend could be unsustainable. That's why it's good to see Deswell Industries paying out a modest 39% of its earnings. Yet cash flow is typically more important than profit for assessing dividend sustainability, so we should always check if the company generated enough cash to afford its dividend.

Check out our latest analysis for Deswell Industries

Click here to see how much of its profit Deswell Industries paid out over the last 12 months.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Stocks with flat earnings can still be attractive dividend payers, but it is important to be more conservative with your approach and demand a greater margin for safety when it comes to dividend sustainability. If earnings fall far enough, the company could be forced to cut its dividend. With that in mind, we're not enthused to see that Deswell Industries's earnings per share have remained effectively flat over the past five years. Better than seeing them fall off a cliff, for sure, but the best dividend stocks grow their earnings meaningfully over the long run.

The main way most investors will assess a company's dividend prospects is by checking the historical rate of dividend growth. Deswell Industries has delivered 3.6% dividend growth per year on average over the past 10 years.

Final Takeaway

Is Deswell Industries an attractive dividend stock, or better left on the shelf? It's disappointing to see earnings per share have fallen slightly, even though Deswell Industries is paying out less than half its income as dividends. It's also paying out an uncomfortably high percentage of its cash flow, which makes us wonder just how sustainable the dividend really is. Overall it doesn't look like the most suitable dividend stock for a long-term buy and hold investor.

Having said that, if you're looking at this stock without much concern for the dividend, you should still be familiar of the risks involved with Deswell Industries. To that end, you should learn about the 4 warning signs we've spotted with Deswell Industries (including 1 which is concerning).

data.title: Is ANZ Group Holdings (ASX:ANZ) Above Fair Value On Its New York Fed Removal?
data.description:
ANZ Group Holdings (ASX:ANZ) has been removed from the New York Federal Reserve's list of banks used for direct foreign exchange dealings, a rare shift that raises fresh questions about its global standing.

ANZ Group Holdings shares changed hands at A$38.98 at the last close, with a 90 day share price return of 6.13% and a 1 year total shareholder return of 17.57%. This points to solid medium term momentum despite a 2.21% decline over 30 days.

Scan how other banks handle reputation and risk by reviewing our hand picked 5 resilient stocks with low risk scores alongside ANZ Group Holdings after this New York Fed decision.

For ANZ Group Holdings, the tension is clear. Investors may ask whether this reputational knock creates a better future entry point, or whether the current price already reflects the setback enough to justify paying up today.

Most Popular Narrative: 21% Overvalued

ANZ Group Holdings last traded at A$38.98, while the most followed narrative on Simply Wall St assigns a fair value of A$32.18. This frames the current price as materially higher than that estimate and brings the recent New York Fed decision into sharper focus.

According to Jamesiskindacool, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the narrative leans heavily on current earnings, capital strength and dividends without banking on ambitious upside from integration or margin shifts.

At A$32.162 per share, ANZ (ASX: ANZ) appears reasonably valued based on its current operating performance. Cash earnings per share were 126.1 cents for the six months to 31 March 2026; annualising this figure implies approximately 252 cents per share and a price-to-earnings multiple of around 12.8 times. The most recent 83 cent interim dividend, together with the preceding 83 cent final dividend, represents a trailing cash yield of approximately 5.2% at the assessed price, before considering the partial franking credits.

See why 11 investors see ANZ Group Holdings as 21% overvalued.

The narrative fair value uses a 7.80% discount rate and, when set against the current A$38.98 share price, points to a cleaner earnings and balance sheet story that does not rely on aggressive assumptions for Suncorp Bank integration or future loan growth.

This framing gives you a reference point to judge whether the reputational setback with the New York Fed lines up with the idea that ANZ Group Holdings trades around 21% above that fair value anchor, or whether recent performance and earnings quality still justify paying close to the current level.

Result: Fair Value of A$32.18 (OVERVALUED)

Still, the New York Fed decision and any shift in institutional client activity could challenge the idea that ANZ Group Holdings deserves only a modest earnings-based valuation gap.

Another View On ANZ Group Holdings: Multiples Versus Narrative Fair Value

There is a different lens you can use on ANZ Group Holdings. At A$38.98, the shares trade on a P/E of 16.2x, which sits below the local peer average of 17.8x, yet well above the global banks group on 10.6x and only slightly under a fair ratio of 17.2x. That mix hints at limited valuation slack if sentiment on risk or earnings quality weakens, even before factoring in the New York Fed decision.

data.title: How CXL Memory Demos At Netlist (NLST) Have Changed Its Investment Story
data.description:
• Netlist appointed Noel Whitley as General Counsel and added James Hickey to its Board and key committees, while also showcasing three CXL NVvault memory proof of concept designs for AI and enterprise workloads at SC26 in Chicago.
  • The focus on CXL based NVvault concepts for intelligent tiering, persistent memory, and reuse of DDR4 assets highlights Netlist's effort to address practical memory efficiency and data management needs across AI, HPC, and database environments.
  • Attention now turns to how Netlist's CXL NVvault proof of concept work could influence the broader investment narrative around the business.
Spot 52 AI infrastructure stocks that, like Netlist, are working on the memory and compute backbone for AI and high performance workloads.

What Is Netlist's Investment Narrative?

To own Netlist, you have to believe the business can turn its CXL NVvault concepts and broader memory portfolio into repeatable, commercially relevant demand while managing the capital heaviness of hardware and the lumpiness of licensing. The recent unveiling of CXL proofs of concept speaks directly to that bet. It signals where engineering time and future R&D dollars are going and what kind of AI and data center customers management is trying to court.

In the short term, the bigger operational questions sit around execution and funding, not just product demos. Revenue is forecast to grow 62.4% a year and the firm reports Return on Equity of 59%. Yet the share price is still down 41.3% over 30 days and 38.1% over 90 days, with volatility already flagged as a risk. Bringing back Noel Whitley as General Counsel and adding James Hickey to the board ties directly into two sensitive areas, intellectual property and capital allocation, but neither move changes the fact that Netlist relies on higher-risk funding and has diluted shareholders over the past year.

Even so, there is a less comfortable angle to Netlist’s story that tends to get pushed to the background when talking about AI memory growth and CXL buzz...
